findings.title: Bind every enabled-window poll to the expected foreground switch
findings.observed: A correct after-switch0, an in-window String1 poll for another switch, and a correct terminal1 after the deadline produce settingsReportedEnabled=true and setupObservationSatisfied=true. Wrong element type and background/nonforeground state reproduce the same result.
findings.cause: enabled_samples validates raw value and time without expected switch identity/label/type/state. summary checks metadata on before/after/terminal only, so an invalid poll can supply the only timely enabled sample.
findings.requiredChange: Require expected Settings switch metadata and stable identity on every sample eligible to satisfy the window. Preserve contradictory observations as diagnostic evidence but exclude them from enabled-window success. Add adversarial controls for wrong identifier/label/type/foreground/state and late terminal1.
findings.scopeLimit: All release/carrier/native-qualification fields remain false. Synthetic host input proves a diagnostic witness-verification gap, not an observed native switch failure or release bypass.

findings.title: Bind route-tap evidence to the selected public row
findings.observed: All three route-search snapshots can report identifier and label Unselected public row. Fixed route indices and route-tap markers still progress and setupObservationSatisfied becomes true.
findings.cause: Route progression validates indices/attempts but never binds the tappable route-search observation to the selected row metadata. The summary validates only the three switch snapshots.
findings.requiredChange: Validate the successful route-search/tap witness against the selected public route contract before allowing selected-route success. Preserve failed or missing row observations diagnostically. Treat route-opened separately: the previous selector can legitimately disappear after navigation and must not be required to retain the old row label/identifier.
findings.scopeLimit: The frozen Swift caller selects the three intended labels. This finding concerns host witness verification and truthful route qualification, not evidence of an actual wrong native tap.

findings.title: Enforce ordered host receipt times during replay
findings.observed: A complete synthetic journal starts with receivedUptime100. After sequence1 receivedUptime is changed to99, replay returns a complete successful setup observation without rejection.
findings.cause: Session checks host is finite and before deadline, then only checks host-start<=29. It does not reject negative elapsed time or regressions against the previous accepted host receipt. replay feeds saved receivedUptime into this unchecked clock.
findings.requiredChange: Track the last accepted host receipt time transactionally and reject time earlier than setup start or the last accepted record. Preserve the existing absolute session/diagnostic limits; add complete-journal replay mutations for first and later regressions.
findings.scopeLimit: The real host uses time.monotonic; this finding demonstrates replay accepting contradictory persisted timing, not an observed reversal of the running host clock. It does not show a network-capability or release-authorization bypass.
